chunks.arabic_text: زَيْدُ النَّرْسِيِّ، وَزَيْدُ الزَّرَّادِ، كُوفِيَانِ. رَوَيَا عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ (عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ).

translations.en: Zayd al-Narsi and Zayd al-Zarrad, Kufan. They narrated from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him).

chunks.arabic_text: قَالَ أَبُو جَعْفَرِ ابْنِ بَابَوَيْهَ: إِنَّ كِتَابَهُمَا مَوْضُوعٌ، وَضَعَهُ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ مُوسَى السَّمَّانُ. وَغَلَطَ أَبُو جَعْفَرِ فِي هَذَا الْقَوْلِ، فَإِنِّي رَأَيْتُ كُتُبَهُمَا مَسْمُوعَةً مِنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ أَبِي عُمَيْرٍ.

translations.en: Abu Ja'far ibn Babawayh said: Their book is a forgery, composed by Muhammad ibn Musa al-Sammam. And Abu Ja'far erred in this saying, for I have seen their books heard from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr.

en.summary: This passage highlights a critical debate in Shia hadith criticism regarding the reliability of Kufan narrators Zayd al-Narsi and Zayd al-Zarrad. While Ibn Babawayh dismissed their works as forged by Muhammad ibn Musa al-Sammam, the author refutes this by citing the 'smu'ah' (audited/heard) transmission from the trustworthy Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, thereby establishing their authenticity through direct chain verification.
en.seo_question: Was the book of Zayd al-Narsi and Zayd al-Zarrad a forgery according to Shia scholars?

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (Imam al-Sadiq), peace be upon him
key_terms.أَبُو جَعْفَرِ ابْنِ بَابَوَيْهَ: Abu Ja'far ibn Babawayh, a prominent Shia scholar
key_terms.مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ مُوسَى السَّمَّانُ: Muhammad ibn Musa al-Sammam, the alleged forger
